subject: Replaceability economics & deployment-fit deep dive
messages:
From: Lucia Park <lucia@edgepath.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@edgepath.com
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: replacement economics + runtime fit for EdgePath pilot

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. Procurement asked me to get a side-by-side for pricing and an explicit ‘replaceability’ plan vs our incumbent. High-level ask:

- Total cost delta over 12 months for our current stack -> Redwood (incl. egress, quantized runtime impact).
- Any upfront credits / pilot discounts you can offer for a 6–8 week proof-of-concept.
- Operational lift: on-call, onboarding support, and estimated engineer hours.

We’re also worried about model parity (some sensitive prompts must match within our tolerance window). Can you provide a short path for rollbacks / fallbacks if quality diverges?

Lucia
Procurement, EdgePath

PS — attaching a template our finance team likes (I'll share via Drive in a follow-up).
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Park <lucia@edgepath.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: replacement economics + runtime fit for EdgePath pilot

Hi Lucia — appreciated the thoughtful list. Quick answers up front, full breakdown attached.

Summary bullets:
- 12-month delta: base consumption forecast + estimated egress puts Redwood roughly 18–24% lower than incumbent at median workload given caching and batching. See sheet: tab "12mo_delta".
- Pilot credits: we can commit a $30k pilot credit for the 6–8 week PoC (applies to hosted consumption only).
- Operational lift: 2-week onboarding (Redwood SE support) + 1x week of runbook handover. Estimated 40–80 engineer hours depending on integration tightness.
- Quality guardrails: we propose canary rollout with A/B (10% traffic), automated evals against your golden prompt set, and an automatic fallback to incumbent if regression > 3% on your metric.

I attached a conservative econ comparison (econ_comparison_v1). Jordan, can you add a short note on runtime compatibility (kv-cache/quantization tradeoffs) — that’s the piece Lucia flagged. Marissa, can you call out any contract side-constraints we should be aware of?

Thanks — Rishi
Head of Sales Strategy, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lucia Park <lucia@edgepath.com>
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 08:57:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: replacement economics + runtime fit for EdgePath pilot

Adding the runtime note inline for transparency.

Jordan's runtime summary:
- KV-cache: if EdgePath's workflows have long sessions (avg context > 1.5k tokens) we should enable prefix caching — that reduces tokens served by ~12% on their sample trace. It requires a small stateful route but no code change to models.
- Quantization: the incumbent uses an int8 path with custom kernels; we can match memory profile with our int8-llm quantization but should expect a ~4–6% delta in rare-token probability mass — measurable on edge-case prompts. We recommend the PoC include the 20 most sensitive prompts for evaluation.
- Latency: we expect parity at P95 on the standard config; if they need lower P99 we should propose Dedicated capacity add-on.

Lucia — I attached a short PDF with gap notes and a recommended test matrix (runtime_gap_notes.pdf).

-Jordan
Principal Solutions Engineer
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Lucia Park <lucia@edgepath.com>
Date: Thu, 22 May 2025 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: replacement economics + runtime fit for EdgePath pilot

Couple of commercial clarifications from my side before we send a final package to procurement: 

- Contract mechanics: pilot credit is one-time, non-refundable, applies to hosted usage only. If EdgePath converts within 90 days after PoC finish, we can roll $20k of that credit into a partial prepay credit on the first invoice.
- Cancellation & rollback protection: we can include a 60-day exit window from the conversion date with pro-rated credit return if material regressions are observed and reproduced. Need legal to sign off on SLAs for that language.
- Discounting: we can offer a stepped volume discount that triggers at 500k inference units/month — structure: 5% @ 500k, 8% @ 1M, 12% @ 2M — these are additive to standard list pricing.

I'll draft language for the pilot addendum and share a redline. Rishi — want me to include a clause tying the fallback safeguard to automated eval thresholds so procurement can see it clearly?

-Marissa
Senior Account Executive
From: Lucia Park <lucia@edgepath.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 May 2025 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: replacement economics + runtime fit for EdgePath pilot

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. Procurement and the ML team reviewed the econ and runtime notes. Quick confirmations: 

- EdgePath accepts the $30k pilot credit proposal (we'll sign the pilot addendum once you send the redline).
- We want the fallback tied to the automated eval threshold (please include the exact metric names and triggers in the addendum).
- Can you provide a short checklist of the PoC milestones and success criteria (we'll map them to our procurement milestone payments)?

If you can send the redline + the PoC checklist by Monday morning our internal board wants to kick off governance review next week.

Lucia
